title: Spiking Neural Networks: A Survey
reconciliation_notes: Minor disagreements on extractability levels for methodology claims resolved through discussion. Both annotators agreed on all HIGH extractability claims.

claims.extractability_rationale: Clear quantitative comparison in Results section with explicit accuracy metrics
claims.claim_text: SNNs achieve 99.4% accuracy on MNIST classification with LIF neurons and surrogate gradient training.
claims.evidence_text: Table 3 reports benchmark results: SNN with LIF neurons trained via surrogate gradients achieves 99.4% test accuracy on MNIST, matching ANN baseline performance.
claims.mapping_rationale: Directly addresses scalable SNN training with quantitative accuracy benchmarks

evidence_quality.rationale: Clear benchmark comparison with established dataset

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative energy comparison with clear baseline in benchmark section
claims.claim_text: Neuromorphic hardware implementation of SNNs achieves 100x energy reduction compared to GPU-based ANNs for inference.
claims.evidence_text: Section 5.2: Loihi neuromorphic chip benchmarks show 0.1mJ per inference vs 10mJ on NVIDIA GPU, representing 100x energy improvement at equivalent accuracy.
claims.mapping_rationale: Directly addresses event-driven vs clock-driven efficiency comparison

evidence_quality.rationale: Clear hardware measurement with established comparison baseline

claims.extractability_rationale: Explicit quantitative claim about network sparsity in methodology
claims.claim_text: SNNs exhibit sparse activation with average 5% neuron firing during inference on image classification tasks.
claims.evidence_text: Analysis of activation patterns shows mean firing rate of 5.2% ± 1.3% across test samples (n=10,000), significantly below traditional ANN activation rates of 40-60%.
claims.mapping_rationale: Directly addresses sparse coding efficiency requirement

evidence_quality.rationale: Statistical analysis with sample size and comparison

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative accuracy on standard benchmark with clear methodology
claims.claim_text: STDP-based unsupervised learning achieves 95.0% accuracy on MNIST without supervision.
claims.evidence_text: Spike-timing-dependent plasticity rule combined with competitive learning achieves 95.0% classification accuracy in unsupervised setting (Table 2).
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses STDP mechanisms with quantitative validation

evidence_quality.rationale: Clear benchmark result with established methodology

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative timing comparison with biological reference
claims.claim_text: LIF neuron models with 10ms membrane time constant match biological spike timing within 2ms accuracy.
claims.evidence_text: Comparison with in vivo recordings shows LIF model predictions correlate with biological spike times at r=0.94, with mean absolute error of 1.8ms.
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses temporal dynamics of spike-timing encoding

claims.extractability_rationale: Clear benchmark result with dataset and accuracy
claims.claim_text: SNN achieves 95.5% accuracy on N-MNIST event-based dataset with 4 timesteps.
claims.evidence_text: Table 4: Event-driven SNN processing N-MNIST achieves 95.5% accuracy using only 4 timesteps, demonstrating efficient temporal processing.
claims.mapping_rationale: Directly addresses event-based sensor integration with SNNs

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative claim but requires inference from multiple sections
claims.claim_text: Surrogate gradient methods reduce training time by 30% compared to ANN-to-SNN conversion.
claims.evidence_text: Training convergence analysis shows surrogate gradient methods achieve target accuracy in 70% of the epochs required by conversion methods.
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses scalable training algorithms for deep SNNs

evidence_quality.rationale: Comparison made but methodology details scattered

claims.extractability_rationale: Valid quantitative claim but embedded in discussion
claims.claim_text: Rate coding preserves 90% of information content in sensory encoding tasks.
claims.evidence_text: Information theoretic analysis shows rate-coded representations achieve 90% mutual information with original signal for natural images.
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses sensory transduction into neural spikes

evidence_quality.rationale: Information theoretic analysis but limited experimental detail

claims.reconciliation_notes: Annotator B initially classified as LOW; upgraded after discussion

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative architecture comparison in methodology section
claims.claim_text: Deep SNNs with 8+ layers achieve comparable accuracy to ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10.
claims.evidence_text: ResNet-SNN with 8 layers achieves 91.2% vs ResNet-18 ANN at 92.1% (Table 5), closing the accuracy gap to 0.9%.
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses scalable deep SNN architectures

claims.extractability_rationale: Hardware deployment metric in technical results
claims.claim_text: Intel Loihi processes 1M spikes/second at 30mW power consumption.
claims.evidence_text: Loihi benchmark: 1 million spike operations per second at 30mW static power, measured on standard workload.
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses hardware deployment on neuromorphic chips

claims.extractability_rationale: Clear accuracy result on established benchmark
claims.claim_text: ANN-to-SNN conversion achieves 92.8% accuracy on CIFAR-10 with 32 timesteps.
claims.evidence_text: Table 6: Conversion from trained ANN to SNN yields 92.8% test accuracy on CIFAR-10 using 32 simulation timesteps.
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses scalable training methods for SNNs

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative latency claim in hardware section
claims.claim_text: End-to-end inference latency on neuromorphic hardware is <5ms for image classification.
claims.evidence_text: Measured inference time: 4.2ms from input to classification output on Loihi chip for 28x28 input.
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses hardware deployment latency metrics

claims.extractability_rationale: Qualitative observation without strong quantitative backing
claims.claim_text: SNNs demonstrate inherent robustness to input noise compared to ANNs.
claims.evidence_text: Discussion notes that spike-based processing provides natural noise tolerance through temporal integration.
claims.mapping_rationale: Related to network stability through temporal processing

claims.extractability_rationale: Theoretical claim from introductory section
claims.claim_text: Biological neurons are fundamentally event-driven, processing spikes asynchronously.
claims.evidence_text: Introduction cites biological evidence that neurons communicate via discrete spike events rather than continuous signals.
claims.mapping_rationale: Background claim about neural transduction

claims.extractability_rationale: Clear performance metric with experimental validation
claims.claim_text: DVS gesture recognition achieves 96.5% accuracy with SNN processing.
claims.evidence_text: DVS128 Gesture benchmark: SNN classifier achieves 96.5% accuracy on 11-class gesture recognition (Table 7).

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative comparison across architectures
claims.claim_text: Recurrent SNN improves sequence prediction accuracy by 8% over feedforward SNN.
claims.evidence_text: Sequential MNIST results: recurrent SNN achieves 97.2% vs 89.1% for feedforward architecture.
claims.mapping_rationale: Architecture comparison for sequential processing

claims.claim_text: Temporal coding can encode more information per spike than rate coding.
claims.evidence_text: Theoretical analysis suggests temporal coding has higher information capacity per spike event.
claims.mapping_rationale: Relates to sensory encoding mechanisms

claims.extractability_rationale: Clear quantitative result in benchmark table
claims.claim_text: Spiking ResNet achieves 93.1% accuracy on CIFAR-10 with direct training.
claims.evidence_text: Table 5: Directly trained Spiking ResNet-18 achieves 93.1% test accuracy on CIFAR-10.
claims.mapping_rationale: Scalable SNN training benchmark

claims.extractability_rationale: Quantitative metric in learning rule comparison
claims.claim_text: STDP learning converges 40% faster than backpropagation for pattern recognition.
claims.evidence_text: Learning curve analysis shows STDP reaches 95% accuracy in 60% of the epochs required by BP (Figure 4).
claims.mapping_rationale: Addresses STDP mechanism efficiency

claims.extractability_rationale: General observation in conclusion without data
claims.claim_text: SNNs are well-suited for edge computing applications.
claims.evidence_text: Conclusion: The energy efficiency of SNNs makes them attractive for edge deployment.
claims.mapping_rationale: General efficiency claim

non_extraction_items.text: Future work will focus on scaling SNNs to larger datasets and more complex tasks.
The brain consists of approximately 86 billion neurons connected by trillions of synapses.
Hodgkin and Huxley (1952) developed the first detailed mathematical model of action potentials.
Neuromorphic computing represents a paradigm shift in hardware design.
A spiking neural network is defined as a neural network that uses discrete spike events for communication.
We hope this survey provides a useful reference for researchers entering the field.
Previous work by Maass (1997) established the theoretical foundations of SNN computing.
Exploring hybrid SNN-ANN architectures remains an open research direction.
The membrane potential is the voltage difference across the neuron's cell membrane.
Several commercial neuromorphic chips have been developed in recent years.
